newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares linger at lowest levels since January.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares linger at lowest levels since January.

text.p: The Cairo stock exchange showed no signs of recovery from its lowest levels since January when Egyptian share prices wilted on Tuesday in unremarkable trade.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index sloughed off 1.4 points to close at 333.11. Prices had ended lower all last week and Tuesday's level was the bourse's lowest since January 19 when it closed at 330.01.
Turnover was an average 45 million pounds ($13 million).
Of the 82 shares traded, 42 ended lower and 23 rose.
Investors dabbled in a cross section of banks, cements, mills and housing sector shares.
"There are no fundamentals for the stocks to be trading down. What is driving the market down is the retail investors selling stock," said broker Tareq Lotfy of Intercapital.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development had the highest valued turnover with 4.4 million pounds changing hands. Its share gained a sliver, ending up 0.35 at 215.
"It could be larger retail investors selling to one another or to institutions," said Lotfy. He said that there were several blocks of 2,000 shares or 4,000 shares changed hands at 213.
Export Development Bank of Egypt was flat at 385 pounds in the second highest valued trade of the day, worth 3.2 million pounds.
General Silos and Storage slipped 3.85 pounds to close at 75 pounds in the third highest valued trade of 2.2 million pounds.
Commercial International Bank/CIB rose about half a pound to 69.51 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 448.19 points from 447.97 points on Monday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 248.52 points from 250.14.
